title: NCSA Gets Supercomputing Capacity With $334 Million Schmidt Sciences Grant
gist: Schmidt Sciences is funding a $334M HPE-built, all-Nvidia (Grace-Blackwell NVL4 plus two B300 NVL72 racks, InfiniBand, VAST Data storage) supercomputer called Garnet at NCSA, giving the center roughly 107 petaflops peak FP64 by mid-2027. The deal shows private philanthropy stepping in to supplement NSF HPC funding, at a time when GenAI-driven component inflation limits how much FP64 capacity even $240M of hardware can buy.

insights.claim: Schmidt Sciences' $334 million grant to NCSA splits into roughly $240 million of hardware acquisition for the Garnet supercomputer and about $94 million covering five years of operations and research support.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Roughly 28% of the grant goes to opex, a useful benchmark for total cost of ownership on mid-size academic GPU clusters.

insights.claim: NCSA's Garnet system delivers about 107 petaflops of peak FP64 for roughly $240 million in hardware, or $2.24 million per petaflops, versus $15.64 million per petaflops for the 13.3-petaflop Cray Blue Waters machine — about a 7X price/performance and 8X performance gain over roughly 15 years.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 7X FP64 price/performance gain over 15 years is modest by historical HPC standards, a sign of how FP64 progress has slowed while vendors chase low-precision AI math.
insights.quote: That works out to a mere $2.24 million per petaflops, a factor of 7X improvement in price/performance
insights.locator: Fast forward to the middle of 2027

insights.claim: GenAI-driven demand has pushed prices for GPUs, CPUs, DRAM and networking sharply higher, so an academic center like NCSA would need much more money to field a machine near the top of the Top500 rankings.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: AI demand is crowding out scientific HPC buyers on price, which supports component vendors' pricing power (memory, networking, accelerators) while squeezing public research budgets.
insights.quote: Given the pricing on GPUs and CPUs and DRAM and networking have all gone nuts thanks to the GenAI boom, where too much demand is chasing too little supply

insights.claim: If Garnet matches the peak-to-sustained HPL ratio of TACC's similar Nvidia-based Horizon system, it would rate about 84.5 petaflops sustained and rank around 35th on the November 2026 Top500 list.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A $334M grant now buys only a mid-pack Top500 system, showing how far capacity at the top of the list has moved.

insights.claim: Schmidt Sciences, the research organization created by former Google executive Eric Schmidt, is funding a national-lab-class supercomputer at NCSA, with the stated aim of supplementing government HPC funding rather than replacing it.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Philanthropic capital is becoming a buyer of scientific supercomputers, an additional demand source for HPC vendors that is not tied to federal budget cycles.
insights.quote: the intent of the Schmidt Sciences organization is to supplement government HPC funding, not to replace it
insights.locator: Tim Boerner, principal investigator for the Garnet

insights.claim: Garnet's architecture and vendor choice were made so the system can be expanded over time, and although neither NSF nor Schmidt Sciences has committed to expansion, the author expects NSF may fund added Nvidia systems.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Possible follow-on Nvidia/HPE orders at NCSA; watch NSF budget actions for expansion funding.
insights.locator: Tim Boerner, principal investigator for the Garnet

insights.claim: Unlike traditional NSF machines, Garnet will accept capacity-grant applications from researchers outside the United States, subject to US export controls, with NCSA keeping about 10% of capacity and Schmidt Sciences allocating the remaining roughly 90%.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Privately allocated US compute open to foreign researchers is a new access model that export-control policy will directly constrain.
insights.locator: With the Garnet system, Srikant says

insights.claim: Schmidt Sciences' research priorities for Garnet capacity are AI and advanced computing systems design, biosciences, astrophysics, and climate modeling.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Signals which scientific workloads private HPC funding will accelerate.

insights.claim: Garnet's main partition uses 640 Nvidia NVL4 boards (each node pairing two Blackwell B200 GPUs with one Grace CPU, two nodes per board) and one 800 Gb/sec ConnectX-8 NIC per GPU, linked by Nvidia Quantum-X 800 Gb/sec InfiniBand in a rail-optimized design.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nvidia captures compute, NICs and switching in the deal, showing its full-stack lock-in at HPC centers and not just in hyperscale AI.
insights.locator: In the Garnet system at NCSA, the NVL4 nodes

insights.claim: At small node counts, HPC centers like NCSA keep choosing InfiniBand over Ethernet because of operational experience, keeping Nvidia's InfiniBand business entrenched in scientific computing.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: InfiniBand demand in HPC holds up even as AI clusters move toward Ethernet.
insights.quote: it is not surprising at all that NCSA would stick with InfiniBand over Ethernet given its experience with that high speed interconnect and the relatively small scale
insights.locator: In the Garnet system at NCSA, the NVL4 nodes

insights.claim: Nvidia's Blackwell B300 trades away FP64 performance to boost FP8 and FP4 math for inference, so Garnet uses B300-based NVL72 racks (two racks, 144 GPUs, 72 Grace CPUs) only for its smaller AI inference partition and B200s for FP64 simulation.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nvidia's roadmap is splitting into FP64-capable and inference-optimized parts, so HPC buyers must run split partitions — and FP64 science risks being sidelined by AI-first silicon.
insights.locator: The smaller part of the Garnet machine

insights.claim: Many recent Top500 machines pair Grace CPUs with Hopper H100 or H200 GPUs for FP64 value, and the NVL4 Grace-Blackwell board has become a standard HPC design, with TACC's Horizon the largest deployment to date.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nvidia's Arm-based Grace CPU is winning HPC sockets alongside its GPUs, displacing x86 in scientific systems.
insights.locator: Many of the machines on the Top500 lists

insights.claim: TACC's Horizon supercomputer combines NVL4 partitions with 4,032 Blackwell B200 GPUs and 2,016 Grace CPUs (168.2 petaflops peak FP64) and a 4,752-node Nvidia Vera Arm CPU partition (131.8 petaflops), for about 300 petaflops total.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nvidia is also winning large CPU-only HPC partitions with Vera, extending its share beyond accelerators.

insights.claim: Hewlett Packard Enterprise won Garnet in a competitive bid against one other vendor (the author guesses Dell), continuing HPE's incumbency at NCSA after the earlier Delta and DeltaAI systems.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: HPE keeps winning mid-size academic HPC deals; HPE and Dell are the two system integrators competing for Nvidia-based HPC builds.
insights.locator: Srikant says that NCSA and Schmidt Sciences did competitive bidding

insights.claim: Part of Garnet's $240 million hardware budget buys a VAST Data all-flash storage system with 50 PB raw and likely at least 100 PB usable after data reduction, augmenting NCSA's existing 25 PB DataDirect Networks Lustre file system.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: VAST Data is winning flagship HPC storage at the expense of incumbent parallel file systems like DDN Lustre — a share signal for private-market storage players.
insights.locator: R. Srikant, director of the NCSA
